claims.text: The initial single-phase fcc FeCoNi alloy has high saturation magnetization and coercivity below 100 Oe.
Controlled gas-phase nitriding can incorporate interstitial nitrogen into single-phase fcc FeCoNi.
Nitriding should be conducted at approximately 400–600 °C for 1–2 hours under controlled nitrogen partial pressure.
Rapid quenching after nitriding will preserve the induced lattice distortion without forming a secondary phase.
Interstitial nitrogen will produce a slight tetragonal distortion of the fcc FeCoNi lattice.
Interstitial nitrogen and the resulting distortion will generate localized strain fields.
The localized strain fields will act as pinning centers for magnetic domain walls.
Nitrogen-induced lattice distortion will increase magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Increased magnetocrystalline anisotropy and impeded domain-wall motion will raise the coercive field.
Nitriding will increase coercivity from below 100 Oe to several hundred Oe relative to untreated FeCoNi.
The nitrided alloy will retain high saturation magnetization despite its increased coercivity.
Nitrogen content can be kept sufficiently low to induce distortion while retaining the overall fcc structure and avoiding a significant reduction in saturation magnetization.
The optimal nitrogen content, treatment temperature, treatment time, and quantitative coercivity increase are not yet established.
